title: Processes vs threads
body: Which statement about processes and threads is correct?

options.t: Threads of the same process share its address space and resources; processes are isolated from each other
A process can have only one thread

answer: Threads share memory within a process.
explanation: Shared memory makes inter-thread communication cheap but requires synchronisation; processes communicate via IPC and offer stronger isolation.

title: Deadlock conditions
body: Which is **not** one of the four necessary (Coffman) conditions for deadlock?
explanation: The four conditions are mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption and circular wait. Preventing any one (e.g. acquiring locks in a global order to avoid circular wait) prevents deadlock.

title: Page faults
body: What triggers a page fault in a virtual memory system?

options.t: Accessing a virtual page that is not currently mapped to a physical frame (e.g. not yet loaded or swapped out)

explanation: The OS handles it by loading the page (minor faults need no disk I/O). Excessive major faults cause thrashing.

title: TCP vs UDP
body: Which statement about TCP and UDP is correct?

options.t: TCP is connection-oriented with reliable, ordered delivery and flow control; UDP is connectionless with no delivery guarantees

answer: TCP = reliable stream; UDP = best-effort datagrams.
explanation: UDP suits latency-sensitive traffic (games, voice, DNS); QUIC (HTTP/3) builds reliability and encryption on top of UDP.

title: First step loading a website
body: When a browser loads `https://example.com` for the first time, what must happen before a TCP connection can be opened?

options.t: DNS resolution of example.com to an IP address

explanation: Order: DNS → TCP handshake → TLS handshake → HTTP request/response → parsing and rendering (plus caching at each step).

title: Purpose of the TLS handshake
body: What does the TLS handshake accomplish?

options.t: Authenticates the server via its certificate and establishes shared session keys for encryption

explanation: Certificates are validated against trusted CAs and the hostname. TLS 1.3 completes in one round trip and supports 0-RTT resumption.

title: HTTP/2 multiplexing
body: What is a key improvement of HTTP/2 over HTTP/1.1?

options.t: Multiplexing many concurrent requests over one connection, reducing head-of-line blocking at the HTTP layer

answer: Multiplexed streams over a single connection (plus header compression).
explanation: TCP-level head-of-line blocking remains, which HTTP/3 addresses with QUIC.
